rubric.reason: AC-A3, AC-A4, AC-A6 (compare's WARNING line naming excluded files, the disappearance of the 'recomputed 82' drift line, and the two CLI modes' behavior) and AC-A9 (CONSUMERS registry exclusions for scripts/eval.mjs and .claude/commands/efficiency-report.md carried as a comment) have zero references -- no test name, AC comment header, or EXISTING_TEST_COVERS mapping -- in scripts/efficiency.test.mjs or scripts/validate/checks/timestamp-contract.test.mjs. The manifest defers all four via a non-canonical 'OUT_OF_TESTPAIR_SCOPE' outcome (not one of test-writer's six canonical per-AC outcomes: NEW_TEST_REQUIRED / EXISTING_TEST_COVERS / EXISTING_TEST_UPDATED / OBSOLETE_TEST_REMOVED / REDUNDANT_TEST_REMOVED / AMBIGUOUS) to the plan's own one-time shell VALIDATE blocks (Task 1, Task 2, ## Validation Commands Level 3), which are Implementer-owned, ran once at implement time, and are not maintained test files -- a future refactor of doCompare/CLI dispatch could silently break AC-A3/A4/A6 with no test ever failing. This is not a capability gap: scripts/efficiency.test.mjs already demonstrates the exact subprocess technique needed for A3/A4/A6 (execFileSync against 'node scripts/efficiency.mjs' in the AC-A5 import-safety test), and timestamp-contract.test.mjs already demonstrates the exact array-membership technique needed for A9 (the 'WATCHED_FILES does not include the three deliberately excluded agents/commands' test). Contrast with AC-A14/AC-A15, which the plan's own AC list explicitly designates to a later, separately-run '## Post-implementation gate' -- a legitimate scope narrowing A3/A4/A6/A9 do not carry.
